description:
Bind more sub-workspaces under the HERE-definated workspace (/workspaces/codeam-codespace) and enhance the production-grade AI Platform Fullstack Environment to a high-speed working high-quality base.

PRODUCTION-GRADE HARDENING (high-speed + high-quality base):

   - Dependencies: stdlib-only by default; cryptography as optional extra
   - Entry points: rollout-shield → rollout_shield.cli:main,

title: device-only controller policy: App-controlled Space mode
description:
Add App-controlled-Space operational mode to rollout-shield — a single-authority configuration where ONLY an attested device can sign claims, monitor, and act. Full device connectivity, no human-controller, no multi-controller.

Background: the codeam-codespace repo is meant to pair with a remote device (the codeam-box). The device has a hardware-anchored key (Ed25519 in TPM/HSM, attested via the hardware/ spec). The current state accepts any number of human + device keys, which is fine for shared development but inappropriate for production-rollout spaces where the device is the sole authority.

Deliverables:

1. controller_policy config field:
   - shared (default): human + device keys both permitted; current behavior
   - device-only: ONLY device/hardware-anchored keys can sign claims; human keys rejected
   - human-only: ONLY human keys can sign; device keys rejected (for dev/test spaces)
   - Stored in ~/.rollout-shield/config.json under controller_policy

2. CLI guards:
   - rollout-shield keys new --agent-id X: if controller_policy=device-only, the
     new key must be hardware-anchored (or the command must be passing
     --hardware-anchored). Otherwise rejected with a clear error.
   - rollout-shield claim create --agent-id X: if controller_policy=device-only,
     the agent's most-recent key must have hardware_anchored=True. Reject
     otherwise.

3. New subcommand: rollout-shield space
   - rollout-shield space show: print current policy + statistics (human keys,
     device keys, last claim signer, daemon mode)
   - rollout-shield space set-policy <shared|device-only|human-only>: switch
     policy. Warns and asks for confirmation; backs up config first.
   - rollout-shield space validate: enforces the policy against the current
     state (no orphan non-device keys when device-only; no orphan non-human
     keys when human-only). Returns 0 if consistent, 1 if not.

4. Health check: add a check_controller_policy check to health_checks.py
   that flags policy violations: in device-only mode, alert on any non-device
   claim signer or any non-device key in the registry.

5. Self-heal repair: repair_controller_policy: under device-only, demote
   non-device keys (move to keys_material/quarantine/) — does NOT delete
   them, just disables them. Under human-only, quarantine device keys.

6. Tests:
   - scripts/dev/test-device-only-space.sh: end-to-end test that
     - installs with device-only
     - tries to create a human key (must fail)
     - creates a device key (must succeed)
     - emits a claim signed by device (must succeed)
     - emits a claim 'signed by' a human key (must fail)
   - Add to scripts/test-all.sh or as a separate gate.

7. Docs:
   - protocol/AGENT-IDENTITY.md: short note on the device-only controller mode
   - hardware/PUBKEY-ATTESTATION.md: cross-reference how the device key is
     registered (the hardware-anchored bit)

Acceptance:
- rollout-shield space show displays the current policy
- rollout-shield space set-policy device-only flips the policy + backs up config
- in device-only mode, non-device keys are invalidated for signing
- non-device claims are rejected with a clear error
- health_checks.py detects policy violations
- self-heal can quarantine non-device keys under device-only
- All 3 modes (shared, device-only, human-only) tested end-to-end

title: AI router (parallel-lateral) + benchmarks + self-cycle + First-of-kind generator
description:
Build the AI-assistance layer for rollout-shield:

1. Parallel-lateral router: routes requests to N models in parallel; outputs are combined laterally (consensus / dedup / best-of). The router is the unique IP — most routers pick one model; this one combines.

2. Free-usable HTML dashboard tab: a new 'AI Assistance' tab in the existing dashboard. Static, no API key needed. Shows leaderboard, cycle history, and First-of-kind artifacts. Uses vanilla JS.

3. High-graded benchmark suite: deterministic graders (hash-based, regex-based, JSON-schema-based) that score model outputs offline. No LLM API calls required for the baseline; real models can be plugged in. Persistent leaderboard.

4. Self-cycle engine: each cycle picks the best-graded model, generates content, grades it, updates the leaderboard, and writes a cycle record to persistent state. Cycles accumulate; the system improves (in a deterministic, reproducible way).

5. First-of-kind content generator: produces unique artifacts (poems, code patterns, design slogans, API sketches) that are fingerprinted (sha256) and tagged 'first-of-kind-<short-hash>' so the same artifact is never produced twice. Persisted under ~/.rollout-shield/first_of_kind/ and viewable in the dashboard.

6. CLI surface:
   rollout-shield ai route <prompt>           # run a request through the router
   rollout-shield ai benchmark --model <id>   # run a model against the benchmark suite
   rollout-shield ai cycle                    # run one self-cycle
   rollout-shield ai cycle --count 5          # run 5 cycles
   rollout-shield ai leaderboard              # show benchmark leaderboard
   rollout-shield ai first-of-kind            # generate a new first-of-kind artifact
   rollout-shield ai first-of-kind --kind poem # specify artifact kind
   rollout-shield ai dashboard                # open dashboard AI tab in browser

7. HTTP API (dashboard):
   GET /api/ai/leaderboard
   GET /api/ai/cycles
   GET /api/ai/first-of-kind
   GET /static/ai-assistance.html            # the AI tab

Tech: Python 3 stdlib only. No external API keys needed for baseline (all models are deterministic mocks; real-model integration is a drop-in).

Acceptance:
- rollout-shield ai cycle --count 3 produces 3 cycle records and an updated leaderboard
- rollout-shield ai first-of-kind --kind poem produces a unique poem with a 'first-of-kind-' fingerprint
- Dashboard /ai-assistance.html renders leaderboard + cycles + first-of-kind artifacts
- Re-running first-of-kind for the same prompt + kind produces the same fingerprint (deterministic), but a different prompt produces a different fingerprint
